lastText: File ClosedAn Army Spent Twice, on Both Sides of the LineMajor DefeatItalian High Command, 1940 — 1945End of hostilities: SEPTEMBER 1943 — SPECULATIVE — filed out of sequence, pages missingImmediate AftermathThis file closes on September 1943, a speculative branch's own ending rather than a date the documented record recognizes — six weeks of an Italian army fighting itself that the actual, bloodless transition of July 1943 never had to spend. The human cost of this path runs higher than the historical one at nearly every hinge point — Italy's own wartime dead, roughly 300,000 military and civilian combined split across two governments and a country fought over twice, were already among the higher tolls of any Axis power relative to population. A speculative path with almost no historical footing: the officer corps' actual loyalty to the constitutional monarchy in July 1943 proved deeper than any loyalty to Mussolini personally. What this file records instead is a counterfactual crisis of legitimacy inside the regime's own institutions — one the losing war underneath it would have overtaken regardless of who signed the orders. Wavering and defecting commanders were arrested rather than allowed to declare for the King quietly — Italian units turned on each other in a way the actual, largely bloodless transition of power never required. The Mediterranean question was answered with Malta named the priority in 1940 — an early invasion attempt was thrown back, and the base survive
